note: Allocating cooling by MARGINAL LEAKAGE BENEFIT instead of temperature excess. Built 29 Aug 2026 against Section 10.8 of Photonic_Cooling_Devices___v9.pdf, which makes leakage suppression a first-class objective for spatially-selective cooling. HotGauge/thermal/leakage_targeting.py, 15 tests. Additive: microrefrigeration.py is untouched and every existing output is byte-identical.

the_figure_of_merit.form: B = s_b * (dP_leak/dT)_b   [W leakage saved per W of heat removed]
the_figure_of_merit.why: combines how cheap a block is to cool with how much cooling it is worth; both measured
the_figure_of_merit.s_b: K/W, measured by the planner's own probe
the_figure_of_merit.dP_leak_dT: from leakage_calibration/, this project's measured curve

WHAT_THE_POLICY_CHANGES.current: clipping_plan allocates by TEMPERATURE EXCESS -- every block above target, to target
WHAT_THE_POLICY_CHANGES.proposed: allocate a BUDGET by marginal leakage benefit
WHAT_THE_POLICY_CHANGES.verdict: the policy does beat clipping on its own objective, 1.45x to 10.6x more leakage removed for the same watts

BUT_THE_LEVER_IS_SMALL_AND_THIS_IS_THE_P.meaning: a watt of extraction returns at most ~1.7% of itself in leakage, peaking near 360 K
BUT_THE_LEVER_IS_SMALL_AND_THIS_IS_THE_P.consequence: leakage payback ALONE never justifies the cooling. The justification stays on the performance side -- holding the clock, avoiding throttle -- which is what clipping_plan already optimises.
BUT_THE_LEVER_IS_SMALL_AND_THIS_IS_THE_P.so_the_settled_decision_needs_a_SECONDAR: docs/PHASE0_CHECKLIST.md records 'extraction is spatially matched to power density' as settled. That decision conflates PROJECTION (a block's removal lands on the tiles above it -- geometry, correct, guarded by TestExtractionTracksPowerDensity, untouched here) with ALLOCATION (how much each block gets). Only allocation is in question, and the measurement says it should gain a leakage tie-breaker rather than be replaced.

A_NON_OBVIOUS_RESULT.what: the most valuable block to cool is NOT the hottest one
A_NON_OBVIOUS_RESULT.why: the measured curve's local doubling constant is 10.7 K at 360 K but 13.3 K at 380 K -- the relative leakage response peaks in the middle of the range, not at the top. At equal leakage the allocator prefers a 360 K block over a 380 K one.

AND_IT_CURRENTLY_CHASES_AN_ARTEFACT.what: every scenario sends its watts to `core_other` -- the McPAT unallocated slab that P0.5f identified as 22%% of core area with no counterpart on a real die (published residual 1.35%%).
AND_IT_CURRENTLY_CHASES_AN_ARTEFACT.why: that block has the most leakage because it has the most unallocated area and power
AND_IT_CURRENTLY_CHASES_AN_ARTEFACT.consequence: a leakage-targeted policy is only as good as the per-block leakage attribution, and ours puts the most leakage in a block that does not exist. Same root cause as the results-broadcast-bus defect in P0.5g: McPAT's per-block outputs are self-consistent only at McPAT's own block sizes.
AND_IT_CURRENTLY_CHASES_AN_ARTEFACT.so: fixing per-block power attribution is the shared prerequisite for BOTH this policy and the ISA comparison -- it is one blocker, not two.

THE_LIMIT.why: McPAT rejects temperatures outside 300-400 K, so the calibrated curve clamps below 310 K. The allocator refuses to cool a block past that rather than chase the clamp.
THE_LIMIT.cost_of_the_refusal: small -- the measured benefit has nearly vanished by 315 K anyway
